2609.18525.title: TRIPROBE: Probing Task Separability Beyond Classification for XAI
2609.18525.paper_summary: Modern evaluation of learning pipelines often reduces to downstream accuracy, leaving open the question of why tasks succeed or fail. TriProbe addresses this gap with a multi-level probing framework for explainable diagnosis of task separability. Rather than treating models as black boxes, TriProbe traces how separability evolves across inputs, learned features, and final classifiers. It decomposes multi-task problems into binary subtasks and applies three complementary probes: a Foundational Probe on input spaces, a Latent Probe on feature representations, and a Final Probe on classifier outputs. Using Maximum Fisher's Discriminant Ratio as a principled separability metric, TriProbe identifies bottlenecks and affected task pairs. Experiments on the Roshambo sEMG benchmark show how TriProbe reveals hidden breakdowns, guiding data collection, validation, and architecture design.
2609.18525.paper_summary_zh: 現代對學習流程的評估通常簡化為下游準確性，留下了為何任務成功或失敗的問題。TriProbe 通過一個多層次的探測框架來解決這一空白，以便對任務可分性進行可解釋的診斷。TriProbe 並不將模型視為黑箱，而是追蹤可分性如何在輸入、學習特徵和最終分類器之間演變。它將多任務問題分解為二元子任務，並應用三個互補的探測器：對輸入空間的基礎探測器、對特徵表示的潛在探測器，以及對分類器輸出的最終探測器。使用最大費舍爾判別比作為原則性的可分性度量，TriProbe 確定瓶頸和受影響的任務對。在 Roshambo sEMG 基準上的實驗顯示 TriProbe 如何揭示隱藏的故障，指導數據收集、驗證和架構設計。
